locations.name: Los Angeles

src.agency: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA)
src.table: California City and County Sales and Use Tax Rates

locations.lead: Los Angeles charges one of the highest combined sales tax rates of any large city in California.
notes: Los Angeles County raised its countywide rate to 9.750% when Measure A replaced the earlier Measure H district tax.
The City of Los Angeles adds no separate city district tax on top of the county rate, so the city and countywide figures match.
Neighbouring cities in the same county can still be higher — several have passed their own district taxes.

locations.name: San Jose

src.agency: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA)
src.table: California City and County Sales and Use Tax Rates

locations.lead: San Jose is one of the few California cities where the combined sales tax rate reaches a round 10%.
notes: San Jose sits 0.250% above the Santa Clara County rate because the city levies its own district tax on top of the countywide districts.
The city of Santa Clara, immediately next door, is lower than San Jose despite being in the same county.
Several Santa Clara County cities share San Jose's rate; others stop at the county figure.

locations.name: Orange County

src.agency: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA)
src.table: California City and County Sales and Use Tax Rates

locations.lead: Most of Orange County sits at the countywide 7.750% rate, but seven cities have added district taxes that push them higher.
notes: 7.750% is the rate in unincorporated Orange County and in the majority of its 34 cities.
Four cities — Los Alamitos, Santa Ana, Seal Beach and Westminster — reach 9.250%, a full 1.500% above the county baseline.
Because district taxes are set city by city, the correct rate depends on the delivery address, not on the county alone.

locations.name: Sacramento

src.agency: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA)
src.table: California City and County Sales and Use Tax Rates

locations.lead: The City of Sacramento sits a full point above the unincorporated Sacramento County rate.
notes: Sacramento County's baseline rate is 7.750%; the City of Sacramento adds city district taxes to reach 8.750%.
Suburbs such as Elk Grove and Rancho Cordova set their own district taxes, so rates vary across the metro.
The state capital's rate applies to the city limits, not to every address with a Sacramento mailing address.

locations.name: Anaheim

src.agency: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA)
src.table: California City and County Sales and Use Tax Rates

locations.lead: Anaheim charges the Orange County baseline rate with no additional city district tax.
notes: Anaheim has not adopted a city district tax, so it matches the 7.750% Orange County baseline.
Anaheim is meaningfully cheaper than nearby Santa Ana and Westminster, both at 9.250%.
The Anaheim Resort district — Disneyland, the convention centre and surrounding hotels — is inside the city limits and uses the same 7.750% rate.

locations.name: San Francisco

src.agency: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA)
src.table: California City and County Sales and Use Tax Rates

locations.lead: San Francisco is a combined city and county, so a single rate applies everywhere inside the city.
notes: San Francisco is both a city and a county, so there is no separate unincorporated county rate.
The rate has moved several times in recent years as district taxes were added and expired — always check the effective date on any figure you find.
Neighbouring San Mateo and Alameda county cities are frequently higher than San Francisco itself.

locations.name: Costa Mesa

src.agency: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA)
src.table: California City and County Sales and Use Tax Rates

locations.lead: Costa Mesa charges the Orange County baseline rate, with no city district tax added.
notes: Costa Mesa has no city district tax, so it sits at the 7.750% Orange County baseline.
South Coast Plaza and the rest of Costa Mesa's retail corridor use this same 7.750% rate.
Adjacent Santa Ana is 1.500% higher, which is a real difference on a large purchase.

locations.name: Austin

src.table: Texas Sales and Use Tax Rates — city rate table

locations.lead: Austin charges 8.25%, the maximum combined rate any Texas city is allowed to levy.

components.label: Texas state sales and use tax

notes: Texas caps total local sales tax at 2.000% on top of the 6.250% state rate, so 8.250% is the legal ceiling.
Austin reaches that ceiling with a 1.000% city tax plus a 1.000% Austin MTA transit tax.
Because the cap is binding, essentially every city in the Austin metro charges the same 8.250%.
